properties.statement: [BL-139] import_graph validates whole nodes, so the adopt loop's corrective re-import is exactly where it breaks
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Found 2026-08-01 by an /adopt pass over music_graph, a ~11k-LOC Python research repo taken from an empty graph to 134 nodes / 379 edges. Reported in that project's own reflow2_feedback.txt.* Re-importing an existing Requirement carrying only {lineage: \"derived\"} fails with *Requirement.statement: required property is missing*. create_node merges \u2014 its own description says *\"a partial props object edits\"* \u2014 and import_graph does not. The adopt workflow is import \u2192 detect \u2192 correct \u2192 re-import, so the mismatch lands precisely on the corrective step the skill prescribes. Adjacent to [BL-133], where two independent readings concluded statements were write-once: the edit path exists and keeps being invisible, and here it is invisible on the *bulk* door specifically. Fix shapes: make import_graph merge like create_node, or say plainly in the tool description that import documents must carry complete nodes. The second is honest and cheap; the first is what the workflow actually wants. Size S \u2014 HALF DELIVERED 2026-08-02; the other half is ANTHONY'S and is recorded as dec:import-merges-or-demands-whole-nodes (proposed). The row's own judgement was *\"the second is honest and cheap; the first is what the workflow actually wants\"*, so the cheap half shipped: import_graph's description now says plainly that each node must be COMPLETE, and that this differs from create_node where a partial props object edits. The merge half was NOT built on my signature, and the measurement says why it should not be. It crosses THREE published boundaries \u2014 ifc:core-api, ifc:graph-export, ifc:mcp-tools \u2014 reported by propagate_from(\"art:export\") at 705 impacted nodes and independently by this session's propagate_change at 723, both naming exactly those three. That trades the migration and backup jobs this module exists for against a smoother adopt loop.
